scope: Bounded primary-source investigation of released Sekiro attack/threat/TTI weights, general gaming policies/motion models, and additional authorized downloadable gameplay. Does not claim an exhaustive search.
conclusion: No immediately reusable pretrained Sekiro temporal attack/TTI model with documented weights permission and verified broad boss coverage was found. Concrete public weights exist, but identified Sekiro checkpoints have undeclared licensing and narrow/action labels; the strongest explicitly licensed generic gaming policy has no attack/TTI head. Existing eight-source acquisition remains unchanged.

sources.availability: Verified ordinary unauthenticated HTTP 206 bytes 0-31/1974723762. Only a 32-byte access probe was read; whole file not downloaded or hashed.
sources.weights_license: NVIDIA License, restricted to non-commercial research; retain full license/notices on redistribution; derivative use limitation persists.
sources.architecture: 493M parameters, SigLip2 vision backbone plus diffusion transformer; current model reads the last frame only.
sources.documented_targets: 256x256 RGB to gamepad joystick/button action chunks (21x16). Behavior cloning; no published attack phase, weapon contact, TTI, or safe-dodge target.
sources.sekiro_boss_coverage: Not verified; no Sekiro text match in the inspected paper HTML. No all-boss claim.
sources.decision: Possible separate non-commercial research baseline. Not an immediate replacement for the native temporal threat/TTI detector, and not installed.

sources.license: CC BY-NC 4.0 on released action annotations
sources.available_material: Parquet gamepad labels and metadata in 20-second chunks; publisher explicitly states source videos are not included.
sources.label_origin: Synthetic labels generated by an in-house model from controller overlays; not direct instrumented enemy hit/contact events.
sources.decision: Does not provide additional downloadable Sekiro footage or TTI gold. Source-video permissions and access would still be needed.

sources.available_material: GitHub contents API lists model.resnet.v1, 44794123 bytes, plus labels.csv and image folders.
sources.weights_license: No LICENSE at repository root and GitHub repository metadata license is null; no explicit weight/data permission located in inspected README.
sources.documented_targets: Single-frame ResNet18 imitation of player IDLE/attack/defend/Mikiri/jump commands from 300x300 enemy crops.
sources.documented_coverage: Author reports Genichiro phase one and human assistance; author describes limited accuracy and missed opportunities.
sources.decision: Weight existence is confirmed, but no reuse/redistribution license inferred from public visibility. Not acquired or integrated. Not a temporal attack/contact model.

sources.available_material: model.resnet.v2 (44796171 bytes) and checkpoint.pth LFS pointer listed in the root.
sources.weights_license: Repository metadata license null; no root license found.
sources.documented_targets: Genichiro-specific attack/state classifier combined with rules and a DQN action policy. Author explicitly reports poor generalization to other bosses.
sources.decision: No licensed ready-made all-boss or contact/TTI model established; no weights downloaded.

sources.available_material: Training code, 30 session label.csv/meta.json pairs; checked tree contains no gameplay frame sequence/video and checkpoints directory only .gitkeep.
sources.decision: Real action metadata exists but corresponding recorded gameplay and trained policy weights are absent in inspected tree. Code-only training path, not new footage or contact supervision.

sources.license: DQN_play_sekiro repository declares MIT; separate older repository permission not established by that license.
sources.available_material: DQN training/testing, screen capture, input and restart scripts; inspected roots contain no model checkpoint or gameplay dataset.
sources.decision: Requires live self-recorded interaction and training. README says bosses can be targeted under matching HUD positions, which is not evidence of a pretrained policy validated on all bosses.

sources.available_material: Author README advertises pretrained models; download script links directly to https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/s/4j4z58wuv8o0mfz/models.zip.
sources.license: Repository BSD-3-Clause; checkpoint-specific archive notices were not separately inspected.
sources.documented_targets: Dense optical flow, evaluated/trained on FlyingChairs, FlyingThings3D, Sintel, KITTI; not Sekiro contact/attack labels.
sources.decision: Potential motion-feature replacement after actual latency/export validation. Published artifact is PyTorch, not a verified ready-made ONNX Sekiro threat model. No weight acquisition/inference performed.

sources.license: Publisher grants use/copy/modify/distribution with full notice and source/publication attribution; already preserved in Dataset/catalog/licenses/LIVE-YT-Gaming.txt.
sources.available_material: Original publisher describes 600 gaming videos and instructs users to submit a form for an emailed download link. No larger public direct Sekiro list was verified in this investigation.
sources.decision: Six existing Q-Bench subset videos remain the actual acquisition. No request form or message sent; no additional videos counted.

sources.available_material: Paper describes 424 original source clips / 74 games, expanded to 4048 codec samples; public website gallery supplies 22 sample rows and direct hosted videos.
sources.permission_evidence: Paper says UGC sources were Creative Commons and PGC directly recorded on PS5; site limits sample usage to academic research. Repository MIT is not treated as overriding site/media-specific terms.
sources.sekiro_coverage: No Sekiro row among 22 published gallery samples. Full download is a request form; full-set Sekiro presence unverified.
sources.decision: Credible future source lead, but adds zero verified Sekiro footage now. No form submission or unrelated-game downloads.

sources.license: Dataset card declares MIT; per-original-creator permission chain was not established in this review.
sources.available_material: Publisher describes 185259 screenshots across 413 titles with image instructions and released VLM checkpoints; public dataset file tree available.
sources.documented_targets: Captions, visual question answering and image-to-JSON; no temporal weapon-contact/TTI labels.
sources.decision: Not ingested: static task mismatch; Sekiro/boss coverage and original-creator permissions not verified. No claim this supplies combat videos.

search_notes: Used GitHub connector repository search and primary repository README, root and tree reads; HF public model/dataset APIs; publisher sites/papers.
HF name search for Sekiro returned the previously known manually gated OpenSIMA04 recordings and OpenSIMA32 dataset. No gate or encryption bypass attempted.
Other inspected SekiroAI hits were game-script decompilation, a Unity combat prototype, or mock/PPO scaffolding; not released vision attack/TTI weights.
Player-action imitation labels do not identify enemy contact time, successful avoidance safety, or one-dodge-per-attack semantics.
integration_change: None; no runtime/training edits, no remote writes or messages to source owners.
